hypothesis: floor-off worlds die of a mating Allee effect: once prey are sparse no mate is within mateRange 200, births stop while food is plentiful. A longer mate range (proxy for a mate call carried further) keeps births going at low density.
prediction: seeds under 80 fall with mateRange, roughly defaults 4-5/8 -> mate-350 3/8 -> mate-500 2/8 -> mate-700/900 0-1/8; population mean rises; hunters alive at the end rises (prey base holds). Risk: at 700-900 the prey boom makes a hunter overshoot or the population pins at maxAgents, and mating share rises at the cost of splits (spec_effective may fall). clonal-off adds little over mate-900. If the dose-response is flat above 500, adopt the smallest value that meets the keep rule floor off (hunters alive >= 12/16, seeds under 80 no more than the defaults) and check it floor on.  (Written before the run, main a363d28, floor off, 8 seeds x 200000 ticks, evals/screens/mate-range.grid.json.)
after: evals/screens/results/mate-range/ (table.md, 6 arms x 8 seeds x 200000 ticks)
note: Ran 2026-11-06, floor off, 8 seeds (means). Seeds under 80 / hunters alive at the end / population mean / predators at end / prey extinctions: defaults 3, 5/8, 233, 30.9, 4.0; mate-350 3, 6/8, 263, 16.9, 5.9; mate-500 4, 5/8, 261, 39.5, 4.3; mate-700 3, 6/8, 245, 34.4, 6.0; mate-900 3, 5/8, 260, 24.6, 7.0; mate-900-clonal-off 7, 2/8, 127, 2.8, 10.9. The prediction failed: a longer mate range lifts the population mean about 12% but does not lower the count of collapsing seeds, and which seeds collapse changes from arm to arm (seed 313056 is 0 in the defaults and 88 to 144 at 350, 700 and 900; seed 637535 is 443 in the defaults and 0 at 700 and 900). Floor-off worlds sit near a tipping point and a lever moves which ones tip. Lifting the clonal cap is a disaster (7/8 collapse, prey extinctions 10.9). The T64 reruns picked two seeds that collapsed under the defaults and tested the lever on them: a selection bias, since a coin-flip seed is likely to survive a rerun with any change. Collapsing worlds boom to about 415 to 475 agents (the cap is 500) by about 30k to 50k ticks and crash within about 20k ticks; survivors swing between about 250 and 500. T64 also found intake per agent falls at low density (155 at 31 agents, 440 at 427), a foraging Allee effect. Next: T66 diagnoses the boom-to-cap crash and the low-density intake. Also measured: eval.hunter_birth_source_share.spec-flip is 0.077 in the defaults (8% of hunter births are a hunter born to a non-hunter mother).
